messages:
Ethan: quick follow-up from the all-hands launch segment  wanted to capture a few clarifying Qs about capacity signals and admission control.

Priya: thanks  two quick ones: 1) what's our target buffer ratio per region during promo spikes? 2) do preemptible GPUs count towards burst pool?

Ethan: short answers: buffer target is 12% of steady-state capacity for prod regions during business hours, 6% off-hours. preemptible/spot show up in burst pool but marked low-reliability; routing avoids them if latency-sensitive.

Lina: can you explain how admission control behaves when a region hits its buffer threshold? is it soft-shed, backpressure, or immediate 429s?

Ethan: admission control steps: 1) soft-queue (tiered timeouts), 2) degrade model variant if policy allows, 3) route to fallback region, 4) return 429 if all options exhausted or customer opted out.

Omar: what's the visibility story for customers? will they see a metric that indicates "in-fallback" vs "served-locally"?

Ethan: yes  we'll emit route-level traces and a boolean tag `x-rw-fallback` plus percent of tokens served remotely. console will surface a per-route chart next sprint.

CTO_Jane: quick product question: for enterprise customers that require strict data residency, how are we guaranteeing fallbacks won't move compute to another jurisdiction?

Ethan: for pinned customers we honor `data_residency: strict` and will not route out of jurisdiction; instead we either queue longer or return a controlled error depending on their `fallback_policy`. Ops teams can also set region allowlists.

Priya: side Q: can teams opt into aggressive quantization automatically during load, or is that manual?

Lina: Optimize is working on an opt-in policy `auto_quantize: true` for routes; it will perform safe-step quantizations (8bit -> 4bit) with canary checks. ETA next week for docs.

infra-bot: [alert] Autoscaler thresholds updated by @Ethan  change-id: 5482  diff: https://redwood.internal/infra/changes/5482 :information_source:

Omar: any blockers for the FRA roll? I've been hearing about networking limits.

Ethan: networking quotas are mostly cleared; remaining item is the regional caching edge for KV-store warmup. we plan a pre-warm job during canary to avoid cold-kv hits.

Priya: good. can we get an operations blurb for support that says what to tell customers when failover happens? a 2-line script would be ideal.

Ethan: will draft a 2-line support blurb and post in #customer-success by EOD.

Lina: also proposing we add a small smoke test that runs at 5m intervals for each region and logs a `region-health` metric so dashboards show green/yellow/red.

Omar: agree  that'll help oncall triage.

CTO_Jane: actionable asks for leadership follow-up?

Ethan: 1) post per-region GPU snapshot tomorrow AM, 2) publish 2-line customer blurb for support, 3) land `auto_quantize` docs and safe mapping, 4) add `x-rw-fallback` and `region-health` metrics to console roadmap. tagging @Lina @Priya for owners.

Priya: ack, will own the customer blurb.

Lina: ack, I'll coordinate with Optimize for the quantization mapping.

Omar: I'll add the 5m smoke test to the canary runbook.

Ethan: thanks all  please react if anything else should be added. :thumbsup:

Priya: :thumbsup:

Lina: :eyes:

Omar: :rocket:
